court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: Inspector General of Registration and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. P. Harish, GA
judgment_text:
Writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking for issuance of a writ of mandamus to direct the 4th respondent herein to register the sale deed dated 14-1-2026 executed by the vendors in favour of the petitioner in respect of the property comprised in Old Survey No. 46/9, New T.S. No. 75/1 Ward F, Block 20 measuring an extent of 1980.25 Sq.ft situated at Boothamur Village, Virudhachalam Taluk Cuddalore district which was presented for registration based on Temporary Number TP/246631803/2026 dated 5-3-2026 within a time frame to be stipulated by this court.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

Abdul Quddhose, J.:— This writ petition has been filed seeking for a direction to the fourth respondent to register the sale deed dated 14-1-2026 to be presented by the petitioner for registration, in respect of the property morefully disclosed in the prayer to this writ petition.

2. Mr P. Harish, learned government advocate, accepts notice on behalf of the respondents, and on instructions, submits that once the sale deed is presented by the petitioner for registration, the fourth respondent shall take a decision as to whether the said sale can be registered or not.

3. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of by directing the fourth respondent to receive the sale deed to be presented by the petitioner for registration in respect of the subject property, and take a final decision as to whether the said deed can be registered or not, within a period of four weeks from the date of presentation of the sale deed by the petitioner for registration. In case, the four respondent decides to refuse to register the sale deed, the fourth respondent shall issue a refusal check slip assigning reasons as to why the said sale deed cannot be registered. No Costs.
